question: What condition governs the practitioner's conduct during puraścaraṇa when the pīṭha becomes visible?
premises: visibility of the pīṭha is conditional
the verse sets a rule for that moment
inference: The practitioner's conduct during puraścaraṇa is qualified by whether the pīṭha is seen.
uncertainties: the exact consequence of pīṭha-sight is not stated in this verse
the relation to the prior day-night rule is implicit
plain_english: But at the time of puraścaraṇa, if there is sight of the pīṭha.
